The origin refused automated retrieval, so the text is carried from an archived copy of the identical address of **10 Aug 2026**. *Mission definition (verbatim)*: “**Prometheus provides an AI platform that helps accelerate nuclear power plant design, licensing, manufacturing and operations to reduce deployment time and costs**”; “**Prometheus is a transformative effort within the Department of Energy Genesis Mission initiative to accelerate nuclear energy deployment**”; “Nuclear power plants have historically faced long development timelines and burgeoning costs, limiting America's ability to deliver affordable, resilient and reliable energy as demand grows”; “The initiative brings together DOE national laboratories, universities and commercial partners to reduce reactor deployment timelines by applying AI, engineering models and advanced computing across the reactor lifecycle.” *Lineage & Mission structure (verbatim — the register's only first-party statement of the ModCon origin)*: “**Prometheus is a Phase II project** … **Prometheus started as a seed model team under ModCon and has since been awarded Phase II funding**”; the Mission “consists of **four primary coordinated efforts**” — **ModCon** (led by Argonne, “to align data and AI models to tackle the nation's science and engineering challenges”, “undertaking the data and model-building activities outlined in **Section 50404 of the OBBB Act (P.L. 119-21)**”, funding central activities “as well as for **seed model teams**”), **AmSC** (led by Oak Ridge, “to provision and deploy computing infrastructure and base platform capabilities to enable the Genesis Mission across the DOE laboratory complex”), an **AI for national security component**, and **Phase I and Phase II projects** on “**nine-month and three-year timeframes**”, “[a] select number of Phase I projects will graduate to Phase II projects.” *Organisation (verbatim)*: “**Prometheus is organized into five research workstreams — platform and AI infrastructure; design and licensing; manufacturing and construction; autonomous operations; and data curation and preparation. Each of these are led by a technical lead who reports to the project lead. A technical integration council of the project lead, deputy project lead, chief scientist and all technical leads meets weekly to manage cross-workstream dependencies, and the project operates under an adaptive management policy that allows resources to be reconfigured as the technology and science develop.**” *Five platform capabilities (headings & wording)*: **AI-Accelerated Design and Licensing** (“generate, analyze and verify reactor designs while preparing traceable licensing documentation for DOE and the NRC”); **AI-Enabled Manufacturing and Construction** (“manufacturing planning, construction sequencing and inspection to shorten production timelines”); **Autonomous Operations** (“monitor operations, detect anomalies and recommend actions **while maintaining human oversight**”); **Governed AI Platform** (“the production-scale AI foundation … through a **governed orchestration layer and persistent digital thread** connecting design, licensing and construction … integrates with DOE's **Genesis Mission Platform** and commercial AI tools”); **Nuclear Knowledge Base** (“**Converts decades of DOE nuclear data into a searchable knowledge base for AI-assisted engineering**”). *Key Facilities (verbatim listings)*: **INL** — Advanced Test Reactor, Materials and Fuels Complex, Transient Reactor Test Facility, Neutron Radiography Reactor; **ORNL** — Manufacturing Demonstration Facility, Frontier supercomputer; **ANL** — Mechanisms Engineering Test Loop, Aurora supercomputer; **SNL** — nuclear energy safety and security test beds. *Targets & verification*: “**Prometheus is designed to cut reactor deployment timelines and operating costs in half**”; three **Elementor counters** — **10×** “Reduction in design and licensing workflow time”, **3×** “Reduction in manufacturing cycle time”, **50 %** “Reduction in operational staffing requirements” — whose numerals live **only in `data-to-value` attributes** (static page prints `0`), i.e. **targets, not measurements**, with **no benchmark, baseline dataset, measurement protocol, validation case or date** printed; the compensating commitment, quoted as the register's **only first-party Prometheus benchmarking policy**: “**Every AI advantage claim is measured against a documented non-AI baseline established before an AI-assisted workflow is used. Prometheus publishes its benchmark suites, baseline datasets and evaluation protocols through the Genesis Mission Platform at each major milestone so results can be independently reviewed and reproduced.**” *Cost share & governance (verbatim)*: “Industry partners have committed **more than $200 million in cost share and $30 million in capital**, proprietary design data and commercial deployment pathways” (FAQ: “more than $200 million in cash, in-kind support, computers, software and data, including **over $30 million in direct cash funding** to national laboratory and university research”); priorities “shaped through the **AI for Nuclear Energy Consortium, a commercially governed body in which Tier 1 members (contributing at least $10M in cash and in-kind resources) hold a seat on the consortium's board of directors**, and an **advisory board** of other member companies contributes **use cases and independent assessments each quarter**.” *Delivery model (verbatim)*: prototype “built and validated under seed funding”; “the **production platform is targeted for initial deployment on the Genesis Mission Platform by March 2027**, with transferable platform specifications … targeted later in the year”; “**software-as-a-service (SaaS) model within the Genesis Mission's American Science Cloud**”, also via “**AWS Marketplace and Microsoft Azure Marketplace**”; “The Prometheus platform is **containerized and packaged as a separately deployable system**”, so utilities, reactor vendors and fuel-cycle operators “can run it within their own cloud tenant or on-premises infrastructure, **keeping proprietary data behind their own firewall**”; the objective being “to deliver a **commercial-grade product in a commercially hosted environment for industry-first use**”, i.e. “a **software entity within the DOE ecosystem** attempting to deliver a product for external users”, extensible “via **standard agent templates, the platform API, and common exchange protocols**”, integrations governed by “technical interoperability standards (e.g., APIs, containerization)”, IP-protective “licensing terms” and “compliance with DOE security and safety requirements”; data security “will follow DOE and industry best practices”; IP “will follow DOE guidelines and partnership agreements.” *Partnership composition & roster (verbatim)*: “a **public-private partnership uniting four DOE national laboratories** (Idaho, Argonne, Oak Ridge and Sandia national laboratories), **four universities** (North Carolina State, Penn State, University of Tennessee, Knoxville and University of Texas at Austin), and the **AI for Nuclear Energy Consortium**”;
